benefits: Pick colors three ways: spectrum canvas, RGB sliders, or sampling from an uploaded image.
Outputs HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK — every format with a copy button.
The spectrum canvas shows the full hue/saturation field at your current lightness.
Image sampling reads the exact pixel you click — a real eyedropper.
Runs entirely in your browser — no uploads, no accounts.

faqs.a: Click any color in the spectrum to set its hue and saturation; the lightness slider then controls brightness. The RGB sliders below give exact channel control, and the image sampler reads real pixels from a photo you upload.
faqs.q: How do the three picking methods work together?

faqs.a: The spectrum is drawn at 50% lightness by default so every hue shows at full strength. Move the lightness slider after picking to darken or brighten the result — the picked hue and saturation are preserved.
faqs.q: Why does the spectrum look brighter than my picked color?

faqs.a: Yes — upload any image (up to 10 MB) and click anywhere on it. The tool reads that exact pixel's color. It is a genuine eyedropper implemented with canvas pixel sampling.
faqs.q: Can I pick a color from a photo?

faqs.a: The EyeDropper browser API exists but is not supported everywhere, so this tool uses canvas-based picking instead, which works in every modern browser without special permissions.
faqs.q: Why not use the browser's built-in eyedropper?

faqs.a: No — images are read into browser memory and pixels are sampled locally. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
faqs.q: Is my uploaded image sent anywhere?

color-picker.formula:
Spectrum pixel: hsl(x/width x 360, 1 - y/height, current lightness)
RGB sliders set channels directly (0-255)
Image click: readImageData(x, y) -> exact pixel RGB
all other formats derived from RGB via standard conversions
howTo: Click anywhere on the spectrum canvas to pick a hue and saturation.
Use the lightness slider to darken or brighten the picked color.
Fine-tune with the red, green and blue sliders for exact channels.
Optionally upload an image and click it to sample a real pixel.
Copy the HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV or CMYK value you need.
keyFacts: The spectrum maps hue horizontally (0-360 degrees) and saturation vertically.
The lightness slider applies to spectrum picks without changing hue or saturation.
RGB sliders cover the full 0-255 range per channel.
Image sampling reads the exact clicked pixel via canvas getImageData.
All five output formats are recomputed from the current RGB on every change.

limitations: The spectrum is drawn at fixed lightness steps; very dark or bright picks need the slider.
Image sampling reads one pixel — noisy JPEG edges may vary by a channel or two.
No alpha/transparency picking; output is always opaque.
Canvas color picking uses the sRGB space only.

color-picker.tagline: Pick from a spectrum, tune RGB sliders, or sample any pixel from your own image.
color-picker.workedExample:
The default color is #4f46e5.
RGB: the hex pairs 4f, 46, e5 are 79, 70, 229 -> rgb(79, 70, 229).
HSL: hue ~243 degrees, saturation ~75%, lightness ~59% -> hsl(243, 75%, 59%).
HSV: value = 229/255 = 90%, saturation = (229-70)/229 = 69% -> hsv(243, 69%, 90%).
CMYK: K = 1 - 0.898 = 10%, C = 66%, M = 69%, Y = 0%.
Clicking the spectrum at the same hue/saturation with 59% lightness reproduces this exact color.
